title: Flat base change of adequate moduli spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal X/k$ an algebraic stack, and $Y,T$ algebraic spaces over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose the diagonals of $\mathcal X,Y,T$ over $k$ are quasi-compact and separated: every scheme test of a diagonal is an algebraic space whose structural map is quasi-compact and whose relative diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and let $g:T\to Y$ be flat. Flatness is tested on etale scheme charts by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then the projection $\phi_T:\mathcal X\times_Y T\to T$ from the $2$-fibre product is an adequate moduli space. There is no finite-type hypothesis and no requirement that the quasi-coherent algebras quantified over on $\mathcal X\times_Y T$ descend from $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Section 2 conventions; Proposition 5.2.9(1), printed p.27; its proof uses Proposition 4.2.1(6) and flat base change. Primary text read online https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Every algebraic space $F$ over $k$, regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid, is an algebraic stack in the sense of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]: an fppf sheaf is an etale stack, its diagonal is representable by schemes and hence by algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and its representable surjective etale scheme atlas is smooth because etale morphisms are smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. This applies to $Y$, $T$, the $U_i$, $T_i$ and $W_{ij}$ below, so all of them may serve as the stacks of the cited stack lemmas. Hence, by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], $\mathcal X_T$ and its further base changes are algebraic stacks. Adequacy includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]; these properties persist under base change by [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism]. In particular all the projections considered below are qcqs. Choose a jointly surjective etale family of affine schemes $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to Y$: take an etale scheme presentation from [def-trf-algebraic-space] and its affine open cover from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so these affine refinements remain etale by the composition statement cited below. The spaces $T_i=T\times_Y U_i$ exist, and $(T_i\to T)$ is an etale covering, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Choose likewise affine etale presentations $(W_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}S_{ij}\to T_i)_j$. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], the composites $(W_{ij}\to T)_{i,j}$ form a jointly surjective etale family. For fixed $i,j$, put $\mathcal Z_i=\mathcal X\times_Y U_i$ and $\mathcal Z_{ij}=\mathcal Z_i\times_{U_i}W_{ij}$. The latter identifies with $\mathcal X_T\times_TW_{ij}$: both groupoids have objects given by an object of $\mathcal X$, a point of $W_{ij}$, and their specified isomorphism over $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(1), reduction to affine etale charts; algebraic.tex Tag 04T2, stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 050F and 050V, spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F.

proof.text: The etale-locality statement [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] applied to the covering $(U_i\to Y)$ shows that $\phi_i:\mathcal Z_i\to U_i$ is an adequate moduli space. Its affine criterion gives both the canonical isomorphism $R_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal Z_i,\mathcal O)$ and global power lifting for every surjection of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal Z_i$. By [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion], this last property says that $\phi_i$ is adequately affine. All criteria apply because $\phi_i$ is qcqs by Step 1.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.1.8(3); Proposition 5.2.9(1), first sentence of proof.

proof.text: The map $T_i\to U_i$ is the base change of the flat map $g:T\to Y$. Every map between algebraic spaces is representable by algebraic spaces, since its pullback by a scheme is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Therefore [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] applies: $T_i\to U_i$ is flat, $W_{ij}\to T_i$ is etale hence flat, and the composite $W_{ij}\to U_i$ is flat. These endpoints are affine schemes, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], applied to the whole source and target as affine opens, says that $R_i\to S_{ij}$ is a flat ring homomorphism. No finite presentation of $g$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(1), flatness in the second sentence of proof; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XC and morphisms.tex Tag 01U5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-affine-target-base-change] with affine target $U_i$, adequately affine $\phi_i$, and the map $W_{ij}\to U_i$. It gives adequate affineness of $\phi_{ij}:\mathcal Z_{ij}\to W_{ij}$. By [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion], for every surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal Z_{ij}$ and every $b\in\Gamma(\mathcal Z_{ij},\mathcal B)$ there are $N>0$ and $a\in\Gamma(\mathcal Z_{ij},\mathcal A)$ mapping to $b^N$. The base-change lemma quantifies over algebras on the new stack itself, so no descent of $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal B$ to $\mathcal Z_i$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(6) for an affine target, as used in Proposition 5.2.9(1); Lemma 4.1.8(3).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections] to the qcqs map $\phi_i$, the flat algebra $R_i\to S_{ij}$ of Step 3, and $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z_i}$. The restriction of this structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z_{ij}}$, directly from its value $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ on every object over a scheme $V$ in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Thus the canonical comparison gives
$$\Gamma(\mathcal Z_i,\mathcal O)\otimes_{R_i}S_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal Z_{ij},\mathcal O).$$
Using the canonical isomorphism in Step 2, its source identifies with $R_i\otimes_{R_i}S_{ij}=S_{ij}$. The scalar-section lemma says explicitly that $1\otimes s$ maps to the structural section pulled back from $s$. Hence the resulting isomorphism is the canonical structure map $S_{ij}\to\Gamma(\mathcal Z_{ij},\mathcal O)$, rather than merely some abstract isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(1), second sentence of proof; stacks-cohomology.tex Tags 0765 and 0771(4), degree zero; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WK.

proof.text: For every $i,j$, Step 4 supplies the global power condition and Step 5 supplies the canonical structural isomorphism over the affine scheme $W_{ij}$. The affine criterion of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] therefore proves that $\phi_{ij}$ is an adequate moduli space. Apply the etale-local assertion of that same node to the jointly surjective family $(W_{ij}\to T)$ constructed in Step 1. Since $\phi_T$ is qcqs and its base changes are the $\phi_{ij}$, it is an adequate moduli space. All power tests in this argument quantify over arbitrary quasi-coherent algebras; the only application of flat scalar extension was to the structure sheaf.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(1), conclusion, with Definition 5.1.1 and the affine criterion of Lemma 4.1.8(3).
